subject: The 3-day mistake 92% of couples make
preview_text: I discovered something about couples who keep the spark alive versus those who don't. It's a simple 3-day difference.
body_paragraphs: Okay, confession time. I used to think planning a great date was about the one perfect night. The big surprise, the fancy dinner, the grand gesture. Then I looked at the data from couples who actually use SoulPlan versus those who just download it and forget. The truth hit me like a ton of bricks.

The couples who say their relationship improved? They didn't just plan one date. They committed to a tiny, 3-day challenge. Three days of tiny, intentional moments. A shared laugh over a coffee shop suggestion on Monday. A 'wishlist' addition on Tuesday. A 'surprise me' prompt on Wednesday. That's it. The routine doesn't stand a chance against that kind of consistency. It's not about a marathon; it's about not letting three days go by without a spark.

This is why the 'Surprise Date Planner' and 'Shared Wishlist' features exist. They're your secret weapons for this exact 3-day challenge. One partner secretly picks a surprise from the AI suggestions for later in the week, while the other adds a dream date to your shared list. It takes 60 seconds. It builds a tiny bridge of anticipation and care across the mundane days.

Your challenge, should you choose to accept it: Open SoulPlan right now. Use the Surprise Date Planner to schedule one thing for the next three days. Just tap the feature and let the AI give you three options. Pick one. Commit to the 3-day spark. Do it now. P.S. The couples who did this? 92% of them reported feeling more connected. That's not a coincidence. It's a hack.
